easy.explanation: The verse says, “Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion.”
easy.q: Where does praise wait for God?

easy.explanation: The psalm calls God “thou that hearest prayer.”
The verse says, “unto thee shall the vow be performed.”
easy.q: What shall be performed unto God?

medium.explanation: The verse connects God’s hearing prayer with all flesh coming unto Him.
medium.q: Why will all flesh come unto God?

medium.explanation: In this context, “waiteth” means awaits or is ready for God.
medium.q: What does “waiteth” most nearly mean in “Praise waiteth for thee”?

medium.explanation: “All flesh” is a broad expression referring to all humanity.
medium.q: What does the phrase “all flesh” refer to?

answers: They are all expressions of worship toward God
challenge.explanation: The passage presents praise, fulfilled vows, and prayer as ways of approaching God.
challenge.q: What connection is made among praise, vows, and prayer?

answers: Only the people of Sion may pray
People everywhere may turn to God
challenge.explanation: The phrase “all flesh” shows that God’s invitation extends beyond one particular group.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “unto thee shall all flesh come”?

answers: Praise and vows, followed by prayer
challenge.explanation: The verses mention praise and the fulfillment of vows, then describe God as the hearer of prayer.
challenge.q: Which sequence best follows the ideas in these verses?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Iniquities prevail against me.”
easy.q: What is said to prevail against the speaker?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “our transgressions, thou shalt purge them away.”
easy.q: What will God do with the transgressions?

easy.explanation: The blessed person is caused to approach God “that he may dwell in thy courts.”
easy.q: Where may the chosen person dwell?

medium.explanation: The passage responds to prevailing iniquities with God’s power to purge transgressions away.
medium.q: Why can the worshipper have hope despite his sins?

answers: To be chosen and brought near to God
medium.explanation: The passage says, “Blessed is the man whom thou choosest, and causest to approach unto thee.”
medium.q: What does the worshipper desire after speaking of forgiveness?

medium.explanation: The phrase means to remove or cleanse away the transgressions.
medium.q: What does “purge them away” mean in this passage?

answers: From awareness of sin to nearness and blessing
From the sea to the mountains
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from prevailing iniquities to being chosen, brought near, and satisfied in God’s house.
challenge.q: What movement of thought occurs in verses 4–5?

answers: Contentment in God’s presence and goodness
A desire to leave God’s house
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes spiritual satisfaction in God’s house and holy temple.
challenge.q: What does being “satisfied with the goodness of thy house” express?

answers: The ends of the earth and those far away upon the sea
challenge.explanation: God is called “the confidence of all the ends of the earth, and of them that are afar off upon the sea.”
challenge.q: Who is described as having God as his confidence?

paragraphs.title: God’s Power over Creation and the Nations

easy.explanation: The verse says that God “by his strength setteth fast the mountains.”
easy.q: What does God set fast by His strength?

easy.explanation: God “stilleth the noise of the seas” and the noise of their waves.
The verse says, “They also that dwell in the uttermost parts are afraid at thy tokens.”
easy.q: What do the people in the uttermost parts feel at God’s tokens?

answers: They are all under God’s power
They are all sources of water
They all dwell in God’s courts
medium.explanation: God establishes the mountains, stills the seas, and controls the tumult of the peoples.
medium.q: What do the mountains, seas, and peoples have in common in this passage?

answers: Those in distant places are afraid
medium.explanation: The verse directly says that people in the uttermost parts are afraid at God’s tokens.
medium.q: What is the result of God’s tokens?

medium.explanation: “Stilleth” means calms, quiets, or brings to silence.
medium.q: What does “stilleth” mean in “stilleth the noise of the seas”?

answers: God rules both natural forces and human unrest
The sea and the people produce crops
The nations live inside the mountains
challenge.explanation: The verse places the noise of the seas beside the tumult of the people, showing God’s authority over both.
challenge.q: What idea connects stilling the sea with stilling the tumult of the people?

answers: God’s signs are recognized even in distant places
The signs belong only to the temple
challenge.explanation: The response of distant inhabitants shows that God’s tokens are visible and powerful beyond one location.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the phrase “at thy tokens”?

answers: Their outgoings are made to rejoice
They are commanded to leave the earth
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “thou makest the outgoings of the morning and evening to rejoice.”
challenge.q: How does the passage end in relation to morning and evening?

paragraphs.title: Rain, Abundance, and the Fertility of the Land

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Thou visitest the earth, and waterest it.”
easy.q: What does God do to the earth?

easy.explanation: The verses describe water, settled furrows, softening showers, and blessed vegetation.
easy.q: What helps the earth’s vegetation spring up?

easy.explanation: The final verse says, “The pastures are clothed with flocks.”
easy.q: Which animals appear at the end of the passage?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “thou blessest the springing thereof” after describing the water and showers.
medium.q: What happens when God waters the ridges and settles the furrows?

medium.explanation: The passage mentions the pastures, valleys, little hills, and pastures of the wilderness.
medium.q: What parts of the land are filled with blessing in this passage?

answers: A long groove in cultivated soil
medium.explanation: A furrow is a groove or row made in soil for cultivation.
medium.q: What is a “furrow” in this context?

answers: God’s water prepares the earth to produce corn
Water is used only by the sea
challenge.explanation: The passage says that God’s river is full of water and that He prepares the earth for corn.
challenge.q: How are water and harvest connected in the passage?

answers: God fills the year with blessing
The year is marked by drought
challenge.explanation: The image of crowning presents the year as surrounded and honored by God’s goodness.
challenge.q: What does “Thou crownest the year with thy goodness” mean?

answers: Water, vegetation, harvest, flocks, and rejoicing
Sin, forgiveness, prayer, and the temple
challenge.explanation: The passage progresses from watering the earth to vegetation, corn, flocks, and joyful singing.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the growth of blessing in the passage?
